decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 7-3. Dissenting: Richard W. Fisher, Narayana Kocherlakota, Charles I. Plosser.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August indicates that economic growth remains slow.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that economic growth so far this year has been considerably slower than the C…”

changes.quote: Recent indicators point to continuing weakness in overall labor market conditions, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Indicators suggest a deterioration in overall labor market conditions in recent months, and the unemployment rate has moved up.”

changes.quote: Household spending has been increasing at only a modest pace in recent months despite some recovery in sales of motor vehicles as supply-chain disruptions eased.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has flattened out, investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.”

changes.quote: Inflation appears to have moderated since earlier in the year as prices of energy and some commodities have declined from their peaks.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “More recently, inflation has moderated as prices of energy and some commodities have declined from their earlier peaks.”

changes.quote: Temporary factors, including the damping effect of higher food and energy prices on consumer purchasing power and spending as well as supply chain disruptions associated with the tragic events in Japan, appear to account for only some of the recent weakness in economic activity.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee also decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that economic conditions--including low rates of resource utilization and a subdued outlook for inflation over the medium run--are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through mid-2013.
Moreover, there are significant downside risks to the economic outlook, including strains in global financial markets.
This program should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates and help make broader financial conditions more accommodative.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.89% APR costs about $53.71 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.88% and moved -7 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.12% would fall by about $12.17 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9%, and employers added an average of 141k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.8% over the past year (August 2011); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.52% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 48%, cut 51%, hike 1%.
